The student was using HKU's course-selection system to choose his courses before the deadline. That evening, something other than a simple glitch, deadline, hack, or full classes caused every course he had selected to vanish. The most consistent reading of the clues—combined with the standard "turtle soup" twist pattern—is that the student's courses were removed because his selections were never actually saved as registered enrollments: the system showed them as chosen, but the evening's event (such as a synchronization/confirmation failure in the selection process) meant they did not persist. By the time he checked, all of his course slots were empty, so it appeared that "all of my courses were gone in one evening."

Did the student's courses vanish because the course-selection system treats selections as temporary until a payment or deposit is made, and the payment failed that evening?

The student was using HKU's online course-selection system before the deadline. He had made his course choices and believed they were set, but the selections were only in a temporary/unsaved state on the system—never actually committed as registered enrollments. When the system synchronized or the session ended that evening, the unconfirmed choices did not persist, leaving his course list empty. So from his point of view, all of his courses had been "gone in one evening": not cancelled by others, not lost to a system crash, hack, deadline, full classes, or his own intentional dropping, but because the choices were never properly saved to the server as final enrollments. When he checked, every slot was blank, and the courses he wanted appeared to have vanished in a single evening.
